title: Separate bounded monic relations commute with adjoining restricted series
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. For integers $r,s\ge0$ put $T=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_rangle$ and $D=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r,Y_1,\ldots,Y_sangle$, the restricted-series rings [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with Gauss norm $\|\sum a_
u X^
u\|_G=\sup_
u|a_
u|$. Let $P=T[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]$ be the ordinary polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], included in $D$ by its coefficients. For each $1\le i\le s$ choose $d_i\ge1$ and coefficients $a_{ij}\in T$ for $0\le j<d_i$, with $\|a_{ij}\|_G\le1$, and set $f_i=Y_i^{d_i}+\sum_{j<d_i}a_{ij}Y_i^j$. Write $J_P=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subset P$ and $J_D=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subset D$ for the generated ideals, and use quotient algebras [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The canonical map $P/J_P\longrightarrow D/J_D$ induced by $P\hookrightarrow D$ is an isomorphism of $T$-algebras. The empty family $s=0$ and $r=0$ are included; the $f_i$ may have repeated roots.

source.place: Section 1.2 Theorem 8 (Weierstrass Division), printed pp.12–13, and Proposition 14 proof, printed pp.15–16, polynomial/Tate quotient comparison for a Weierstrass polynomial. This is the agent-formulated extension to several separate monic relations. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For each $i$, put $A_i=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r,Y_1,\ldots,\widehat{Y_i},\ldots,Y_s\rangle$. Relabel the exponent coordinates to put $Y_i$ last; this preserves the cofinite decay condition, every finite Cauchy-product coefficient, and the Gauss norm. The regrouping in [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] therefore identifies $D$ with restricted series in $Y_i$ over $A_i$. Apply [lem-trf-tate-weierstrass-norm-division] to $g=f_i$: its leading coefficient is $1$, its lower coefficients have norm at most $1$ even in $A_i$, and its upper tail is zero. Denote the unique decomposition by $h=Q_i(h)f_i+R_i(h)$, where $R_i(h)\in A_i[Y_i]$ has $Y_i$-degree less than $d_i$. Uniqueness applied to sums and to multiplication by an element of $A_i$ proves that $Q_i,R_i$ are additive and $A_i$-linear. It also gives $R_i(f_i h)=0$, by comparing with the decomposition having quotient $h$ and remainder zero.

source.place: Section 1.2, Theorem 8, printed pp.12–13: unique division, specialized to the bounded monic polynomial; coordinate relabelling and linearity written explicitly.

proof.text:
The operation $R_i$ preserves a previously imposed bound $\deg_{Y_j}<d_j$ when $j
e i$. Indeed write such an input as the finite sum $\sum_{k<d_j}Y_j^k h_k$ with $h_k\in B=K\langle X,Y_\ell:\ell
e jangle$. Extracting one $Y_j$-coefficient preserves restrictedness, directly from the cofinite decay definition. The polynomial $f_i$ belongs to $B$ because all its coefficients belong to $T$. Apply [lem-trf-tate-weierstrass-norm-division] in $B$, with $Y_i$ last, to each $h_k$: write $h_k=q_k f_i+r_k$ with $\deg_{Y_i}r_k<d_i$. Substitution gives a decomposition of the original input in $D$, with quotient $\sum_{k<d_j}Y_j^k q_k$ and remainder $\sum_{k<d_j}Y_j^k r_k$. Uniqueness of division in $D$ identifies this last sum with $R_i(h)$. Its $Y_j$-degree is still less than $d_j$. For any $j
e i$ we also have $R_i(f_j h)=f_jR_i(h)$: here $f_j\in A_i$, so this is exactly the $A_i$-linearity established in step 1.

source.place: Agent finite-coordinate argument using Section 1.2, Theorem 8, printed pp.12–13; this is why the separate-variable hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Set $h_0=h$ and $h_i=R_i(h_{i-1})$ for $1\le i\le s$, and put $N(h)=h_s$. Step 2 inductively shows that $N(h)$ is supported in the finite box $0\le\alpha_i<d_i$ in the $Y$-exponents. Grouping this finite box gives $N(h)\in T[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]=P$. Telescoping the equations from step 1 gives $h-N(h)=\sum_{i=1}^s Q_i(h_{i-1})f_i\in J_D$. Moreover $N(f_jh)=0$ for each $j$: reductions with index $i<j$ retain the factor $f_j$ by step 2, reduction with index $j$ kills it by step 1, and later reductions preserve zero. Additivity then gives $N(J_D)=0$, since the generated ideal consists of finite sums $\sum_j f_jb_j$. Thus every class modulo $J_D$ has a representative in $P$.

source.place: Agent finite iteration of Theorem 8; several-variable extension of the quotient comparison in Section 1.2, Proposition 14 proof, printed pp.15–16.

proof.text: For a polynomial input $p\in P$, each division in step 1 actually has polynomial quotient as well as polynomial remainder. To see this without invoking an additional division theorem, view $p$ as a polynomial in $Y_i$ over $T[Y_j:j\ne i]$, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. If its degree is $n\ge d_i$ and its leading coefficient is $b$, replace it by $p-bY_i^{n-d_i}f_i$. The leading term cancels, and the degree strictly decreases. Iterating ends with a polynomial remainder of $Y_i$-degree less than $d_i$, and the subtracted terms record a polynomial quotient. If the input is zero or has degree less than $d_i$, take quotient zero. These finite polynomial decompositions are also decompositions in $D$, so uniqueness in [lem-trf-tate-weierstrass-norm-division] identifies them with $Q_i(p),R_i(p)$. Induction through the reductions therefore gives $p-N(p)\in J_P$.

source.place: Elementary descending-degree polynomial algorithm and Theorem 8 uniqueness; compare Section 1.2, Proposition 14 proof, printed pp.15–16.

proof.text: The inclusion $P\hookrightarrow D$ sends every $f_i$ to the corresponding generator, hence induces the stated $T$-algebra homomorphism $\phi:P/J_P\to D/J_D$ with the quotient convention [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. It is surjective by step 3. For injectivity, if $\phi([p])=0$, the quotient-kernel description gives $p\in J_D$ and hence $N(p)=0$ by step 3. Step 4 then gives $p=p-N(p)\in J_P$, so $[p]=0$. An explicit inverse on classes is $[h]\mapsto[N(h)]$: additivity and $N(J_D)=0$ give independence of the representative, while steps 3–4 give both inverse identities. This inverse preserves multiplication and scalars because $\phi$ does and is injective: apply $\phi$ to each required identity and cancel. If $s=0$, the reduction is the identity, $P=D=T$ and both ideals are zero. If $r=0$, $T=K$ and every division above still applies. No step uses distinct roots, separability, or reducedness.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-baf0e0663 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the report and all six cited statements in full. The delivery is one commit with no new nodes. The statement is unchanged and true; the parent cites it with the same hypotheses. I tested it on: s=0 and r=0; d_i=1; f_i=Y_i^d; repeated roots (Y-a)^d with |a|<=1. Y-p^{-1} over Q_p shows the coefficient norm bound is needed. Step 1: lem-trf-tate-weierstrass-norm-division applies over A_i (tail zero, lower coefficients of norm <=1 in T, contained in A_i). It is complemented by the regrouping in lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion. Uniqueness gives additivity, A_i-linearity and R_i(f_i h)=0. Step 2: f_i lies in B because its coefficients are in T. Division in B followed by uniqueness in D correctly keeps Y_j-degree < d_j, and f_j in A_i gives R_i(f_j h)=f_j R_i(h). Step 3: the box representative, the telescoping into J_D, and N(J_D)=0 by finite sums are all correct. Step 4: monic long division over T[Y_j, j≠i] terminates and, by uniqueness, matches R_i on P, so p-N(p) is in J_P. Step 5: the map is well defined, surjective and injective, and a T-algebra map. Route: both lemmas are in unit sk-i-curve-zero; the rest are definitions, so no tool_uses are needed. Duplicates: I read the closest candidates, including tate-convergent-division, affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison, tate-unit-ball-polynomial-reduction and per-tate-triangular-distinguished-coordinate; none states this. Mathlib: LeanFinder, Loogle, LeanSearch and grep were all run. IsDistinguishedAt.algEquivQuotient covers formal power series only, so there is no leaf. Sources: Bosch §1.2 Thm 8 / Prop 14 is WANTED and not available locally. The proof is marked as an agent proof and I checked the mathematics independently. No SGA source is used. No changes.
